name: Judicial discretion

subjectOf.text: Predictive and generative AI systems threaten fairness by reducing complex judicial processes to statistical correlations, which neglects the emotive and cognitive dimensions of justice and the contextual nuances human judges consider.
subjectOf.abstract: Predictive and generative AI systems often reduce complex judicial processes to statistical correlations, neglecting the emotive-cognitive dimensions of justice.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: AI used for judicial decision-making rather than administrative tasks

subjectOf.text: AI's role in legal practice must remain that of a supportive tool rather than a replacement for human judgment, because AI augments legal practice but cannot replicate the empathy and discretion that responsive judging requires.
subjectOf.abstract: AI's role as a supportive tool, rather than a replacement for human judgment, is critical. As emphasized in multiple studies, AI augments legal practice but cannot replicate the empathy and discretion required for responsive judging.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: judicial and adjudicative functions, as distinct from transactional or administrative legal tasks
